cards.text: God is still speaking to Moses, Israel's leader. He has already described the holy garments for Moses' brother Aaron and Aaron's sons (Exodus 28:2-4). Now He tells Moses how to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Him as priests.

First, Moses is to take a young bull and two rams without blemish. He's also to fill a basket with unleavened bread, cakes mixed with oil and wafers anointed with oil, all made from fine wheat flour, and present it with the bull and the rams. FINE wheat flour, friend. I just stood up a little taller on my base.

Then Moses is to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water. He's to dress Aaron in the garments, from the tunic to the turban with its holy diadem, and anoint him by pouring oil on his head. Then come tunics for Aaron's sons, plus sashes and headbands. Me, I've got ONE apron and ONE hat, friend, and I've been wearing them since the angel called me out of that junk drawer.

cards.question: God says the priesthood will belong to Aaron and his sons only for their own lifetimes.

cards.text: Next, the young bull is to be presented at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head. Moses is to slaughter it before the LORD, put some of its blood on the horns of the altar with his finger and pour the rest at the base. The fat, the lobe of the liver and both kidneys are to be burned on the altar, but the flesh, hide and dung are to be burned outside the camp. It is a sin offering.

Then comes the first ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head too. Moses is to slaughter it, splatter its blood on all sides of the altar, cut it into pieces and wash the entrails and legs. Then he's to burn the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering to the LORD.

cards.question: The first ram is burned whole on the altar as a burnt offering to the LORD. How does God describe it?

cards.text: Then the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head again. Moses is to slaughter it, put some of its blood on their right earlobes, right thumbs and right big toes, and splatter the rest on all sides of the altar. Then he's to sprinkle blood from the altar and anointing oil on Aaron and his sons and on their garments.

cards.question: Moses is to sprinkle blood from the altar and anointing oil on Aaron, his sons and their garments. What does God say this does?

answers.text: It consecrates them and their garments
It protects them from their enemies
It seals a covenant with the tribes

cards.text: Back to the second ram, the ram for ordination: Moses is to put its fat and right thigh, plus one loaf, one cake and one wafer from the basket, in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. Then he's to burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering, a pleasing aroma and a food offering to the LORD.

Moses is to wave the breast of the ordination ram before the LORD too, and that breast will be his portion. Moses gets a portion, and me, I get paid in crumbs, so GOOD for him. Then the waved breast and the lifted thigh of the ordination ram are to be consecrated for Aaron and his sons.

cards.question: The breast and thigh of the ordination ram are a one-time gift to Aaron and his sons, just for their ordination day.

cards.text: Then God looks ahead past Aaron: his holy garments will belong to his sons after him. The son who takes his place as priest must wear them for seven days.

cards.question: Aaron's holy garments will belong to his sons after him. What does God say the garments are for?

answers.text: So his sons can be ordained in them
So the people will remember Aaron
So they can be stored in the tent

cards.text: Moses is to boil the ordination ram's meat in a holy place, and Aaron and his sons are to eat it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting with the bread from the basket. No outsider may eat it, and anything left until morning is to be burned up. Leftovers? In MY bakery, a cookie has never once survived until morning, and every clue points to me.

cards.question: God says no outsider may eat the ordination meat and bread. Why not?

answers.text: Because the portion is too small
Because the elders eat it later

cards.text: God tells Moses to take seven days to ordain Aaron and his sons, with a bull sacrificed as a sin offering each day for atonement. Moses is also to purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.

cards.question: Moses is to make atonement for the altar for seven days. Then whatever touches the altar will be ___.

cards.text: Then God gives the daily routine: two lambs a year old every day, one in the morning and one at twilight, each with fine flour, oil and wine. Morning AND twilight, every single day, friend, and some mornings I can't even beat my own snooze button.

cards.question: For the generations to come, the daily burnt offering of the lambs is to be made before the LORD at the entrance to the tent. What does God say will happen there?

cards.text: God says He'll meet with the Israelites there too, and that place will be consecrated by His glory. Then the LORD says He will consecrate the Tent of Meeting, the altar, and Aaron and his sons to serve Him as priests.

cards.question: Once the tent, the altar and the priests are consecrated, God says He will be the Israelites' God.
God says the Israelites will know He is the LORD their God who brought them out of Egypt. Why does He say He brought them out?

answers.text: So He might dwell among them
So they could build Him a city
So they could rule over Egypt

cards.text: God's still got more to tell Moses, friend. Stick around, because this isn't over.
